newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - Brent CFDs lose ground, others hol.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - Brent CFDs lose ground, others hol.

text.p: Brent crude CFDs lost ground for the third consecutive day on Thursday while other swaps held steady or were a touch firmer.
Neutral to timidly bearish API data released last night give little direction, dealers said.
Brent CFDs tracked lower as the main supportive buyer seen earlier in the week and late last week quietly withdrew.
June 2-6 was down to -27 cents against July compared with -22.5 cents while June 9-13 dropped back to -27/28 from -22.5 cents.

Traders said there were offers, but very few bids in a slow market. A Dated Brent cargo was done at -24 cents under July for 8-10 June and a CFD for August was concluded at around -26/27 cents under September.
High sulphur fuel swaps gained $1-1.50 with a June deal at $83 despite physical pricing moves that had barges selling at $79, $80 and $81 fob ARA.
"The lower numbers will not suceed in pulling swaps down, because we have also had physical barges at $82 and $83 and there is good swap buying interest when it nears $80," one dealer said.
Low sulphur swaps were also about $1 stronger with July offered at $95.50 amid very quiet bidding. June was pegged around $95.75.
Light end swaps were steady and quiet, with gasoline in particular waiting for the U.S open.
June gasoline swaps hovered unchanged around $204.50 with June naphtha steady at $189.
